title: The index rebuild says what happened, in the CLI's report and Intent.app's menu
objective:
Rebuilding the search index tells the person who ran it what happened, in the CLI's report and in Intent.app's menu, so that a clean run never reads as a crash (issue 0664).

Concretely:

1. One function in intentsvcs names a language's level-3 state from its stored run and the paths gone stale since: `stale` when a run stored and some of what it stored has gone stale, the extractor's move included; the run's own `missing` or `failed` whatever is stale; `current` only when a run stored and nothing it stored has gone stale. The search envelope's `ResolutionState::of` and intent-cli's `resolution_lines`, which `intent index status`, `intent index rebuild` and `intent index resolve` all print through, both ask it, so no face can name one run two ways (WP-01, cc).
2. `intent index status --json` and `intent index rebuild --json` name that same state for each language, and the text still lists every stale path, as its deliberate rule says (WP-01, cc).
3. `intent index status` and `intent index rebuild`, text and JSON, name when the index was last reconciled, read from the store's own stamp and never from a clock at render (WP-01, cc).
4. Intent.app's Rebuild Search Index row copies Gtools' Refresh Search row: its second line says how long ago the index was reconciled, in Gtools' age words, from the CLI's stamp; a rebuild that fails raises an alert as Gtools' refresh does; every run is still recorded in the app's log, and a rebuild no longer opens the log by itself (WP-02, ic).
5. Each package lands alone with its own judge run, one build carries both, vc tells hv which build that is, and the release stays hv's.
context:
hv filed issue 0664 on 2026-10-31, at 07:08:12Z by its event's stamp: Rebuild Search Index in Intent.app's menu "causes a silent crash only visible when viewing the log", with the log's block pasted into vc's session. vc measured it the same morning, and nothing crashed:

- Every rebuild the app has logged since 2026-10-22, six of them, exited 0 in 21 to 24 seconds.
- No crash report exists for Intent.app or intentd. Both processes were the ones that had run since the evening before, and macOS's log holds no error or fault from the app across the last three rebuilds.
- The block's last line, its exit line, is the verdict: exit 0 in 23.8 seconds. Everything above it is the rebuild's report of what the index holds, and 243 of its lines listed the Rust files changed since rust-analyzer last resolved references, on 2026-09-17.

What made a clean run read as a failure is two defects and one design.

- **The report contradicted itself.** It named Rust's level 3 `current` on the line directly above `stale: 243`, while every search answer named the same run `stale`. Measured live before vc's resolve run: `intent search --json` gave `"state": "stale"` with `"stale_total": 243`, and `intent index status` printed `resolution: rust  current  rust-analyzer`. `resolution_lines` in intent-cli's `render.rs` prints the stored run's `state`, which records what the last run did; `ResolutionState::of` in intentsvcs' `search.rs` derives `stale` for a run that stored and has since gone stale. ST0076's AC-07.1 made one function own the search faces' level-3 words, and the index report was left outside it.
- **Intent.app says nothing about a finished run.** `runLogged` in `IntentApp.swift` records the block in Intent.app.log and then opens that log in the macOS Console, so the report is the only feedback, and the reader has to infer the outcome from its last line. Gtools' Refresh Search row, which hv's rule of 2026-10-22 makes the model for Intent's menu, opens nothing: its second line says how long ago the catalogue was built, and a failure raises an alert.
- **The report lists every stale path by design.** `resolution_lines`' doc comment says the stale paths are listed, never counted, because a reader needs to know whether the file in front of them is one of them. Six weeks without a resolution run made that list most of the output. vc refreshed Rust's references on hv's word at 07:28Z (run 2, stored at 07:28:53Z, joined 575 of 575 files, stale none), so today's list is empty. Any committed change to a Rust file makes that file stale again, and until WP-01 lands the report will again say `current` above it.

hv's ruling, in vc's session and read before 07:26Z by date -u: "Ok, do all of that. Raise it as a new steel thread, assigned to CC (core) and IC (UX/UI), elaborate all of the necessary details and instructions, and then check all of that in and hold." "That" was vc's plan: the report says `stale` whenever files are stale, the menu states each run's outcome, cc builds the Rust and ic the Swift, vc judges each landing without claiming it, a fix hv asked for lands alone with its own run and build, and the release stays hv's.

Out of scope until hv rules: shortening the stale list, which reverses the deliberate rule above; a remedy line under `stale` naming `intent index resolve`; and any change to Run Doctor, which keeps opening the log as Gtools' doctor shows its console.

Issue 0664 closes when both packages are Done and hv has seen the row on the build that carries them. Its title says crash, and retitling it is hv's call as its reporter.

wps.title: One level-3 state on every face, and the index report names its reconcile time
wps.objective: The index report names a language's level 3 the way every search answer does, from one function in intentsvcs, so `intent index status`, `intent index rebuild` and `intent index resolve` can never say `current` above a list of stale files; and the report, text and JSON, names when the index was last reconciled, which Intent.app's row reads in WP-02.
wps.body:
## Builder and judge

cc builds this package and claims `ST0090/01` in the same chain as `intent wp start ST0090/01`, after checking with `intent wb status --json` that no active peer holds it. vc judges it and claims nothing. It lands alone, ahead of ic's WP-02, which reads the reconcile time this package adds.

## What moves

- **One derivation.** Move the rule `ResolutionState::of` applies (intentsvcs, `search.rs`) into one function every face asks: `current` only for a run that stored with nothing stale; `stale` for a stored run with stale paths, which includes the extractor's move because that fills `Run::stale` with every path; and the run's own `missing` or `failed` whatever is stale. `Run::state` keeps recording what the last run did, and no face prints it as the language's state. Where the function lives is cc's call: `index::resolved`, beside `Run`, is the natural home. The search envelope's `ResolutionState::of` and intent-cli's `resolution_lines` both call it.
- **The text report.** `resolution_lines` (intent-cli, `render.rs`), which `intent index status`, `intent index rebuild` and `intent index resolve` all print through, names that state on each language's first line. The stored line, the dropped line, the extractor line and the stale list stay as they are, the list in full.
- **The JSON.** `report_index` serialises `status.resolution`, the raw `Run`, so today its JSON says `"state": "current"` beside a non-empty `stale`. The JSON names the derived state for each language, and the last run's own outcome stays readable as a fact of its own. The field names are cc's call, and a renamed field is named under the next version in CHANGELOG. Measured readers of `index status` output: `the_index_says_what_it_holds.rs`, `every_face_says_what_level_three_knows.rs` and `render.rs`'s own unit tests. No Swift file, no script under `bin/` and no doc quotes the line.
- **The reconcile time.** `index::status::Status` gains the store's `reconciled_at` (`Store::reconciled_at`, stamped by `stamp_reconciled` in `Facade::index_rebuild` and `Facade::index_refresh`), and the report names it in text and JSON. It is a column the reconcile wrote, never a clock read at render (D42, `one_clock.rs`), and an index with no stamp names none. intentd's watcher refreshes stamp the same column, so it says when the index was last brought in line with the tree, not when it was last rebuilt.

## Arms, named before the bank

- A run that stored, with stale paths: the report's first line and the search envelope both say `stale`, and the JSON agrees. `common::level_three`'s fixture already drives `index status` over resolved, failed and unresolved runs.
- The same run with nothing stale says `current`, and the envelope names nothing.
- A failed or missing run with stale paths keeps its own state in both faces.
- The existing pins hold: `the_stored_line_says_how_many_files_the_stored_run_joined` (current, nothing stale), `every_face_says_what_level_three_knows`' failed line, and `the_index_says_what_it_holds`' rule that status and rebuild print one report.
- `index status --json` names a reconcile time after a rebuild and none before one, and the text says the same.

The AT rows cite `native/rust/crates/intent-cli/tests/the_index_report_names_level_three_as_search_does.rs` and `native/rust/crates/intent-cli/tests/the_index_report_names_its_reconcile_time.rs`. Re-cite them with `intent at edit` if the bank names the arms elsewhere.

## The judge, named before the run

One heavy run at the desk, in cc's worktree at the bank's tip: the format check, workspace clippy at `-D warnings`, the intentsvcs and intent-cli suites whole, and `intent critic rust` on every changed `.rs` file (decision 79). After the landing and the build, vc drives the installed pair in this checkout: `intent index status` and its `--json`, and `intent search --json` with one Rust file made stale, reading the state each names.

wps.title: Intent.app's Rebuild Search Index row copies Gtools' Refresh Search row
wps.objective: Intent.app's Rebuild Search Index row tells the operator what happened the way Gtools' Refresh Search row does: its second line says how long ago the index was reconciled, a rebuild that fails raises an alert, and a rebuild no longer opens the log by itself.
wps.body:
## Builder and judge

ic builds this package and claims `ST0090/02` in the same chain as `intent wp start ST0090/02`, after checking with `intent wb status --json` that no active peer holds it. vc judges it and claims nothing. It may bank alongside cc's WP-01 with the CLI stubbed, and it lands after WP-01, whose reconcile time it reads.

## The model is Gtools' row, file for file

hv's rule of 2026-10-22 holds: the menubar apps use one set of controls the same way, and no row is bespoke. Gtools' Refresh Search row is the model (gtools#0066, gtools#0108), in `~/Devel/prj/Gtools/native/macos/Gtools`:

- `CmsStatus.refreshTitle(refreshing:)` gives the title, and the busy caption while the verb runs (`Gtools/Models/CmsStatus.swift`).
- `CmsStatus.refreshSubtitle(status:now:)` gives the second line, `built <age> ago` from the daemon's `built_at`, in `uptimeText`'s words (12s, 5m, 2h 3m, 1d 4h), and nil when the daemon names no time.
- `GtoolsApp.refreshItem()` sets that line as the item's `subtitle`, and `refreshSearch()` raises the alert `Refresh failed` with the error when the verb throws.
- `CmsService.refresh()` runs the CLI and logs to OSLog. Nothing opens a console; only Gtools' doctor shows one.
- `GtoolsTests/CmsStatusTests.swift` pins the title, the caption, and the second line at a set age and with no time.

## What moves in Intent.app

- **The second line.** The Rebuild Search Index item, built by `commandItem` in `IntentApp.swift`, gets a `subtitle`: `reconciled <age> ago`, in Gtools' age words, from the `reconciled_at` that `intent index status --json` names once WP-01 lands, and none when the CLI names none. The verb is the index's own rather than Gtools' `built`, because intentd's watcher stamps the same column after every source edit (`Facade::index_refresh`), so `built` would claim a rebuild that did not happen. The age comes from the CLI's stamp, never from the app's own record of its runs.
- **Where the stamp is read.** At launch, after each rebuild, and on the poll the app already runs if that read can carry it without a second process per poll. The choice is ic's, and the bank names it.
- **A failure.** A rebuild that exits non-zero, or cannot be run, raises an alert titled `Rebuild failed`, as Gtools' `Refresh failed` does, carrying the CLI's own `error:` and `remedy:` lines. Today `runLogged` throws only when the process cannot be spawned, so the exit code has to reach the caller.
- **The log.** Every run is still one block in Intent.app.log, as issue 0607 made it, and the Log item still opens the log. A rebuild no longer opens it by itself, as Gtools' refresh opens nothing. Run Doctor keeps opening it, as Gtools' doctor shows its console, and the comment in `rebuildMenu` that says why stays true.
- The item's title and busy caption do not change.

## Arms, named before the bank

In the shape of Gtools' `CmsStatusTests`: the second line at a set age, and none with no stamp; the title and the busy caption; a stubbed failed rebuild reaching the alert's words with its error and remedy lines; and a stubbed successful rebuild recording its block in the log and opening nothing. The existing `LogTests` arms stay green. The AT row cites `native/macos/Intent/IntentTests/RebuildItemTests.swift`; re-cite it with `intent at edit` if the bank names the arms elsewhere.

## The judge, named before the run

A light run at the desk: the app's test target through xcodebuild, the Swift lint delta against main (the installed critic arms nothing for Swift), and a read of the diff against Gtools' row. Then hv looks at the row on the build that carries both packages, and vc tells hv which build that is.

criteria.text: One function in intentsvcs names a language's level-3 state from its stored run and the paths gone stale since: `current` only for a run that stored with nothing stale, `stale` for a stored run with stale paths, the extractor's move included, and the run's own `missing` or `failed` whatever is stale; the search envelope and the index report both ask it, and no face prints `Run::state` as the language's state.

`intent index status`, `intent index rebuild` and `intent index resolve` name that state on each language's first line, with the stored line, the dropped line, the extractor line and every stale path below it as today, and a search answer's `index.resolution` names the same state for the same run.

`intent index status --json` and `intent index rebuild --json` name the same state for each language as the text does, and the last run's own outcome stays readable as a fact of its own; a renamed field is named under the next version in CHANGELOG.

`intent index status` and `intent index rebuild`, text and JSON, name when the index was last reconciled, read from the store's `reconciled_at` and never from a clock at render, and an index with no stamp names none.

Intent.app's Rebuild Search Index item carries a second line, `reconciled <age> ago` in Gtools' age words, from the `reconciled_at` that `intent index status --json` names, and none when the CLI names none; its title and busy caption do not change.
A rebuild that exits non-zero, or cannot be run, raises an alert titled `Rebuild failed` carrying the CLI's own `error:` and `remedy:` lines, as Gtools' `Refresh failed` does.
Every rebuild is still recorded as one block in Intent.app.log, and a rebuild no longer opens the log by itself, while Run Doctor still opens it.
hv sees the Rebuild Search Index row's second line after a rebuild, on the build that carries WP-01 and WP-02, and vc records which build that was.
